briefs.summary: This tutorial shows you how to use **FastAPI** with most of its features, step by step. It is also built to work as a future reference so you can come back and see exactly what you need.

api.name: fastapi dev
api.summary: Runs the development server in watch mode.

api.name: fastapi run
api.summary: Runs the server in production mode.

api.name: uv add
api.summary: Adds FastAPI with the standard optional dependencies to the project.

api.name: pip install
api.summary: Installs FastAPI with the standard optional dependencies via pip.

api.name: uv init
api.summary: Creates a new Python project with a minimal pyproject.toml.

gotchas: For production use, run the server with `fastapi run` instead of the development command `fastapi dev`.
If you do not want the optional standard dependencies, install FastAPI with `uv add fastapi` instead of `uv add "fastapi[standard]"`.
`uvx` is an alias for `uv tool run`; it runs Library Skills in a temporary isolated environment.

plan_draft.title: FastAPI REST API Plan
plan_draft.overview: Create a minimal FastAPI project with Pydantic models and serve it using uvicorn. The workflow uses uv for dependency management and the FastAPI CLI for development and production runs.

phases.title: Initialize project and add dependencies
phases.body:
- Run `uv init myapi --bare` to create a minimal pyproject.toml[^fastapi-1]
- Add FastAPI with standard extras: `uv add "fastapi[standard]"`[^fastapi-1]
- Add Uvicorn server: `uv add uvicorn`[^uvicorn-1]
- Commit the generated pyproject.toml to version control
- Create a `src/` directory and place code under `src/` to match the module layout
- Ensure the Python interpreter version is compatible with FastAPI and Pydantic (>=3.9)

phases.title: Create FastAPI application skeleton
phases.body:
- Create file `src/main.py`
- Import FastAPI: `from fastapi import FastAPI`[^fastapi-1]
- Instantiate the app: `app = FastAPI()`
- Add a simple health endpoint: `@app.get("/health")\n    def health():\n        return {"status": "ok"}`
- Export the app variable for uvicorn: `__all__ = ["app"]`
- Run a dev server to verify: `uv run fastapi dev`[^fastapi-1]

phases.title: Define Pydantic data models
phases.body:
- In `src/models.py` import BaseModel: `from pydantic import BaseModel, PositiveInt`[^pydantic-1]
- Create a request model, e.g., `class ItemCreate(BaseModel):
    name: str
    quantity: PositiveInt`
- Create a response model, e.g., `class ItemResponse(BaseModel):
    id: int
    name: str
    quantity: int
    created_at: datetime | None`
- Use `model_dump()` when serializing models in responses[^pydantic-1]
- Add `__all__` export for the models
- Run a quick script to instantiate the models and print `model_dump()` to confirm validation

phases.title: Implement CRUD routes
phases.body:
- In `src/main.py` import the models: `from .models import ItemCreate, ItemResponse`[^pydantic-1]
- Add a POST route: `@app.post("/items", response_model=ItemResponse)`
    `def create_item(item: ItemCreate):
        # placeholder logic, assign id and timestamp
        return ItemResponse(id=1, name=item.name, quantity=item.quantity, created_at=None)`
- Add a GET route to retrieve an item by id: `@app.get("/items/{item_id}", response_model=ItemResponse)`
    `def read_item(item_id: int):
        # placeholder return
        return ItemResponse(id=item_id, name="sample", quantity=1, created_at=None)`
- Optionally add PUT/PATCH and DELETE routes following the same pattern
- Ensure each route uses proper type hints for automatic validation

phases.title: Configure production server with FastAPI CLI
phases.body:
- For production, run `fastapi run src/main:app` which starts Uvicorn under the hood[^fastapi-1]
- Verify that the server listens on the default port 8000 or specify a port: `fastapi run src/main:app --port 5000`[^fastapi-1]
- Confirm that the `uvicorn.run` signature matches the example in the docs[^uvicorn-1]
- Add a `scripts/start.sh` that executes the production command for easy deployment
- Test the production command locally to ensure no watch mode is active (GOTCHA: use `fastapi run` not `fastapi dev`)[^fastapi-1]
- Document the command in the README
- After starting, send a request to `/health` to verify the health‑check endpoint works
- Ensure the server shuts down gracefully (e.g., via Ctrl+C) so FastAPI can run any registered shutdown handlers

phases.title: Test and verify the API
phases.body:
- Install `httpx` (or use curl) to send requests to `/health` and `/items` endpoints
- Write a minimal test script that POSTs a JSON payload to `/items` and asserts the response contains the expected fields
- Run the dev server and execute the test script; fix any validation errors reported by Pydantic[^pydantic-1]
- Switch to the production command and repeat the test to ensure identical behavior
- Commit all changes and tag a release version

phases.title: Write pytest tests for endpoints
phases.body: The project uses pytest for testing, but pytest is not covered in the provided library briefs; therefore detailed test implementation steps cannot be specified here. Create test modules under `tests/` that import the FastAPI app and use a test client to exercise each endpoint, asserting status codes and response payloads.

pitfalls: Using `fastapi dev` in production will run the server in watch mode; switch to `fastapi run` for stable deployments[^fastapi-1]
If you install FastAPI without the `[standard]` extras you may miss optional dependencies like `email-validator` required for some features[^fastapi-1]
The `uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker` module is deprecated; avoid it and use the `fastapi run` command or the `uvicorn-worker` package for Gunicorn integration[^uvicorn-1]
Pydantic V2 introduces breaking changes; ensure your code follows V2 syntax or import `pydantic_v1` if you need legacy behavior[^pydantic-1]
Running `uv add uvicorn` installs the server but does not automatically add the optional `uvicorn-worker` package needed for Gunicorn; add it separately if you plan to use Gunicorn[^uvicorn-1]
Make sure the Python version in the `uv` environment satisfies FastAPI and Pydantic requirements (>=3.9); otherwise import errors will occur
